title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 2.71 (versions follow prime numbers; 271 after 269): the living book. Their talk ('dialogo') is a book of her shelf, for her answers and for 'who it is', with her taste for it as for any other book; a line of it is said without its speaker. Her tastes weigh in 'who it is' too: what she finds of a subject weighs by her taste for the book it is in, and the book of what she says first waits for him to follow the talk. The thread helps what he says now, it does not replace it, but when what he says now carries nothing. Measured in a copy: 'el reino de los cielos' -> her books; 'quien es tu papa?' -> her heart; her tastes began to count (a book with N = 2). Stated: the living book was not yet seen answering; what her tastes learn in a long talk is not measured. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v2.71: el libro vivo. Prototipo de investigación.
